entities.summary: Sahier al-Qalamawi was a significant literary figure and politician from Egypt who shaped Arabic writing and culture through her writing, feminist activism, and advocacy. She was one of the first women to attend Cairo University and in 1941 became the first Egyptian woman to earn her Master of Arts Degree and PhD for her work in Arabic literature. After graduating, she was employed by the university as their first woman lecturer. Al-Qalamawi was also one of the first women to hold a number of chief positions including chairperson of the Arabic Department at Cairo University, president of the Egyptian Feminist Union, and president of the League of Arab Women University Graduates.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Suhayr al-Qalamawi's advocacy for women's education and empowerment led to her appointment as the first woman lecturer at Cairo University, paving the way for future generations of Egyptian women in academia. Her trailblazing achievements also inspired a new wave of feminist activism in Egypt.
